# jstack: notes (the lines of 2026-10-28 that defer an action on an event, as the seed pass found them)

- Check command: `make check-fast BASE=origin/main`, while Josh's fast track holds (words 853da9c0377b and e39acf431196, 2026-10-17 22:55 and 22:56 ET: no full local `make check`, CI is the gate). Run it in the turn and wait for it; never end a turn waiting on a test slot. After the fast track: `make check` (ruff check, ruff format --check, pytest on six workers since #339, about 52 s alone). CI runs it on every pull request, on this machine's three runners; three runs at once overload the 12 cores until check-workers-share merges.
- New T3 threads in a main checkout start as a home by themselves: `hooks/home-start.sh`, wired as a SessionStart hook in `~/dotfiles/claude/settings.json`. It is silent in worktrees, outside T3, on resume, in a submodule or a bare repo, in the T3 scratch folder, and in repos with an `off` file (every other repo since pull request 40, one that never had a home included: there the thread is told it is the repo's first home). `/nohome` opts out.
- T3 settles a thread by itself when a pull request linked to it with `link_pull_request` merges. A pull request watch (`watch_pull_request`) wakes the thread on a failed check, passing checks, a comment or a conflict, but not on merge.
- No stacking (the user, 2026-10-10: "wait for the base to merge, then launch"). If a pull request is found stacked on another's branch anyway, it conflicts once its base is squash-merged: `gh pr edit <n> --base main`, then its crewmate rebases with `git rebase --onto origin/main origin/<base branch>`.
- No home arms a watch loop (the user, 2026-10-10: the watch loop goes; `scouts/fewer-messages.md`). A thread messages its home only when the home must act: a crewmate's one `fixed and green` line, a crewmate that ends with no pull request, a scout's End. A thread blocked on the user waits in its own thread ("the waiting state is correct"). Homes do not message each other about merges; a home reads the other homes' plans before a launch.
- Two exceptions from the user (2026-10-10, on the page `reports/ps-playbooks.html`; words in `scouts/ps-playbook-anatomy.md`, "The user's answers on the page"). To "no home arms a watch loop": "an hourly scheduled run through T3's schedule_task, only while a queue is out, removed when it ends". To "no stacking": "take it as written, and allow a stack for this one playbook", for `autopilot-stack` alone. Neither is in a skill until `ps-home-playbooks` merges.
- Traps of 2026-10-13. Never run the whole suite under an outer `flock` of the heavy-suite lock: its browser test takes that lock and the run deadlocks holding it (until cs-browser-lock merges); use `jgauge test-slot -- make check`. `jbus queue add` on a row that exists sets its `--depends` anew and voids its approval: approve again at the same time, and edit a brief before its row launches or tell its crewmate what changed. After 10 passes with no room jbus puts the first waiting row at `gate` and counts it as waiting on him: it asks nothing and launches by itself when the load drops. A scout that has reported still takes a message: ask it for the briefs his picks unlock, with the order and the `--depends`.
